Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

snazzieR 0.1.3

Regression diagnostics

Four new functions cover the checks that follow fitting a model. They reproduce output from base R and car, and car does not need to be installed.

  • diagnostics.plots() draws the four plot(lm) panels (Residuals vs Fitted, Q-Q, Scale-Location, and Residuals vs Leverage with Cook’s distance contours) as a 2 x 2 grid of ggplots in snazzieR.theme(). The most extreme observations in each panel are labelled with their observation numbers, and the labels are placed so they do not overlap each other or nearby points. Each panel is also available on its own through $plots.
  • marginal.model.plots() draws the plots of car::mmps() as one faceted ggplot: the response against each numeric term and against the fitted values, with a loess smooth of the data and a loess smooth of the model’s fitted values. title says which model the plots belong to.
  • unusual.points.table() lists the observations of an lm or glm fit that are high-leverage points, outliers, influential points or bad leverage points. Each row gives the observed and fitted response, leverage, standardized residual and Cook’s distance. flag chooses which criteria count, n.max keeps the rows with the largest Cook’s distances, and id labels the observations.
  • VIF.table() reports variance inflation factors sorted from highest to lowest, with 1/VIF, GVIF, adjusted GVIF (and its df) and a moderate or severe flag. Factors and other multi-df terms get generalized VIFs that match car::vif(). cols picks the columns.

Both tables return LaTeX by default and plain text with latex = FALSE, like the other summary tables.

Table previews in RStudio and Positron

  • LaTeX tables from model.summary.table(), ANOVA.summary.table(), eigen.summary(), pls.summary(), ridge.summary(), format.pls(latex = TRUE), VIF.table() and unusual.points.table() now show an HTML preview when an R Markdown chunk is run interactively, for example with the “Run” button. In 0.1.2 the viewer stayed blank. When a document is knitted, the table goes to knitr as before.
  • The snazzieR.preview option switches the preview between HTML, plain text and the raw LaTeX source. See ?snazzieR_table.

Changes to existing tables

  • The caption argument of model.summary.table(), ANOVA.summary.table() and eigen.summary() is now called title. caption still works as an alias, so existing documents run unchanged.
  • model.summary.table() and ANOVA.summary.table() have default titles (“Model Summary” and “ANOVA Summary”), so title can be left out.
  • model.summary.table() typesets the fitted equation in LaTeX math on its own centered line between the title and the table, for example log(PrizeMoney) = 0.1943 - 0.00353 DrivingAccuracy + .... Negative coefficients are subtracted (0.1.2 printed + -0.004), and coefficients show four significant digits. The title is a plain caption again, so it is centered over the whole table.

Bug fixes

  • model.summary.table() and model.equation() split the equation in two when the response was transformed, as in log(y). One table then had two captions and LaTeX reported a “multiply defined” label.
  • ANOVA.summary.table() gave the Residuals row a :3 significance code although that row has no p-value.
  • model.summary.table(latex = FALSE) printed blank padding rows and a duplicated column of row names in the coefficient table.
  • The significance footnote under model.summary.table() and ANOVA.summary.table() read >0.001 where it meant <0.001.
  • color.ref() restores the user’s graphical parameters on exit.

Dependencies

  • dplyr is no longer imported. The package uses the native |> pipe.
  • graphics, grDevices, grid and htmltools are now declared in Imports, and ggplot2 must be at least 3.5.0.
  • DESCRIPTION gains a BugReports field.
